one_liner: Magento is an ecommerce platform for running storefronts and managing catalogs, inventory, checkout, and orders, available as self-hosted Magento Open Source and commercial Adobe Commerce deployments.

auth.notes: Magento Open Source, Adobe Commerce on Cloud (PaaS), and on-premises Adobe Commerce use signed OAuth 1.0a requests for third-party integrations and document bearer tokens for admin and customer access. Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service (SaaS) uses Adobe IMS OAuth 2 for user-based and server-to-server flows.

access.notes: On a free, self-hosted Magento Open Source store, the store administrator can create and activate an integration without paying Adobe or submitting it for review. Composer installation uses separate Marketplace keys. Adobe's hosted offerings have customized pricing, and the SaaS REST API requires an Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service license and Adobe Developer Console access.

api.notes: REST covers back-office reads and writes, including product management and order processing. GraphQL supports storefront workflows. The SaaS REST API is smaller than the PaaS and on-premises APIs: customer and guest REST endpoints are not available on SaaS, but GraphQL offers similar functionality.

mcp.notes: The maturity rating applies to the installable Commerce Developer MCP for App Builder development and storefront customization, not live-store administration. Adobe separately describes a Storefront MCP for live shopping but does not confirm its rollout status. The third-party thomastx05/magento-mcp project documents a local server for Magento 2 administration.

verdict.rationale: A developer can self-activate an integration on a free, self-hosted Magento Open Source store and use the generated credentials with the documented web APIs. The REST docs cover the full order-processing workflow, so an API-backed toolkit does not depend on the Storefront MCP rollout.

A free Magento Open Source deployment, third-party API integrations, and self-activation with generated credentials establish a self-serve free path. The quotes do not expressly establish every detail about installation or review in the notes.
